title: Generating gastruloids with somite-like structures from mouse embryonic stem cells
protocol: Thaw the bottle(s) of N2B27 at 37 °C in the water bath, shaking occasionally.
Remove bottles from the water bath as soon as ice has completely melted.
Vigorously shake the bottle and store at 4 °C overnight.
The next day, vigorously shake the bottle again and check for precipitates or protein aggregates under a microscope if desired.
Aliquot N2B27 medium into 50 ml tubes (max. 35 ml per tube to prevent leaking).
Store aliquoted medium at -20 °C.
Thaw the required number of N2B27 aliquots 2 days prior to gastruloid formation by placing them on a rotator at 4 °C overnight.
Transfer thawed medium to a T175 cell culture flask 1 day prior to gastruloid formation, and place in the incubator with lid slightly open overnight.
Pre-warm PBS, ESLIF medium, and Trypsin to 37 °C in a water bath.
Aspirate the medium from cells and wash cells twice with PBS.
Add 1 ml pre-warmed Trypsin to well of 6-well plate and incubate for approximately 3 minutes at 37 °C.
Dissociate cells into single-cell suspension using P1000 pipette, transfer to a 50 ml Falcon tube.
Add 4 ml of ESLIF medium to neutralize Trypsin.
Spin down at 200 g for 3 minutes.
Remove supernatant and wash cell pellet with 5 ml PBS.
Spin down at 200 g for 3 minutes.
Carefully remove PBS, add another 5 ml PBS for a second wash.
Spin down at 200 g for 3 minutes.
Remove all PBS without disturbing the cell pellet.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 1 ml N2B27 using a P1000 pipette.
Add a few ml of N2B27 to dilute the cells for counting.
Count cells using a Bürker-Türk counting chamber.
Dilute the cells to the required concentration in N2B27 medium in a new Falcon tube.
Distribute 40 μl of cell suspension into U-bottomed, non-adherent 96-well plates.
Transfer the solution into a sterile tray.
Use a multichannel and DNA LoBind tips to distribute the solution.
Cover the plate with its corresponding lid.
Gently tap the side of the plate to ensure drops are in the center of the wells.
Confirm the presence of cells using a microscope.
Incubate the plate in an incubator at 37 °C, 5 % CO2 for 48 hours.
Prepare 16 ml of N2B27 supplemented with 4.8 μl 10 mM Chiron (final concentration of 3 μM) in a Falcon tube for each 96-well plate.
Pour the medium-Chiron mix into a tray.
Add 150 μl of the medium-Chiron mix to all wells using a multichannel and DNA LoBind tips.
Hold the pipette at an angle, push the pipette tips to the side of the wells, and pipette out the medium with some force.
Dislodge the gastruloids from the plate during this process.
Place the plate in the incubator for an additional 24 hours.
For each plate, prepare 16 ml of N2B27 medium.
Carefully remove 150 μl of medium per well using a multichannel pipette.
Hold the pipette at an angle and slightly press against the wall of the wells to prevent loss of gastruloids.
Add 150 μl fresh N2B27 medium per well using the multichannel pipette.
Use some force to displace the gastruloids from the plate bottom when adding fresh medium.
If necessary, add two times 75 μl instead of one time 150 μl for better displacement of gastruloids.
Repeat steps 21 and 22 at 96 hours after aggregation.
Thaw Matrigel on ice.
Pool the gastruloids in a 5 ml low binding Eppendorf tube on ice.
Replace the N2B27 medium in the tube with fresh cold N2B27.
Add 3.6 ml N2B27 per tube when embedding in 10% Matrigel, and 3 ml per tube when embedding in 25% Matrigel.
Add the correct volume of Matrigel to the tube (400 μl per tube when embedding in 10% Matrigel; 1 ml per tube when embedding in 25% Matrigel).
Mix suspension well by pipetting up and down a few times with a P1000 pipette from which ~3mm of the tip is cut off with sterile scissors.
Distribute 500 μl of this mix per well over 8 wells of a 24-well plate using the P1000 pipette with the tip cut off.
Mix suspension before pipetting into each well to prevent gastruloids from settling at the bottom of the tube.
Leave the plate on the bench for approximately 1 minute so that gastruloids settle to the bottom.
Place the plate in the incubator for an additional 24 hours.
Mix Matrigel with cold N2B27 medium (none for embedding in 100% Matrigel; 50% of the required volume for embedding in 50% Matrigel).
Add 60 μl of the Matrigel-N2B27 mix to each well of a 24-well plate on ice.
Transfer gastruloids one by one into the Matrigel using a P20 pipette.
Incubate the plate at 37 °C for 10 mins to solidify the Matrigel.
Add 500 μl N2B27 medium (37 °C; pre-incubated in the incubator for pH equilibration) to each well after the Matrigel has solidified.
Place the plate in the incubator for an additional 24 hours.
Add PBS0 to the wells without removing the medium/Matrigel.
Remove the medium/PBS0 and wash again with PBS0.
Incubate in 4% PFA/PBS overnight at 4°C by adding ~500 μl 4% PFA/PBS to every well of the 24-well plate.
Wash 3 times for 5 min in PBS-Tween (0.1% Tween-20).
Transfer gastruloids to 1.5 ml DNA LoBind tubes using a P1000 pipette from which ~3mm of the tip is cut off with sterile scissors.
Pipette PBS next to the gastruloids with some force in order to dislodge them if they are still embedded in Matrigel or attached to the bottom of the plate.
Use a spatula to remove the gastruloids from the plate if pipetting does not work.
Scrape the gastruloids from the plate bottom for those grown in 100% Matrigel.
Allow leftover pieces of 100% Matrigel attached to the gastruloids to dissolve after proteinase K digestion and overnight incubation step in hybridization buffer at 68°C.
